subject: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path forward so you can share with finance/procurement:

Summary of ask (from call)
- Primary goal: quantify inference spend per feature so BrightPath can model CAC payback and feature-level margins.
- Initial run-rate estimate discussed: ~20M tokens / month across three prioritized features (Search snippets, Clinical summarization, Personalized recommendations).
- Business target: target $/1M tokens to land somewhere in the low double-digits (you mentioned mid-teens as a ceiling).

Clarifying questions we need to finalize the proposal
1) Can you confirm the monthly token split per feature? (ballpark numbers will do — e.g., Search: 8M, Summarization: 7M, Recs: 5M)
2) Which revenue metric should we use for CAC payback modeling? (ARPU per MAU, ARR per paying account, or contribution per converted user?)
3) Do you have an internal target for $/1M tokens for procurement to approve? You mentioned "preferred low teens" — is $11–13 the range?
4) Any constraints on SLAs/uptime or regional-only hosting requirements?

Attachments: I attached a blank unit_econ_workbook.xlsx with the inputs we discussed and a one-page pricing sketch that maps token tiers to a target $/1M. Please fill the green input cells and return; we will convert to a sensitivity table and final proposal.

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm token split + which revenue metric to use by Wed (4/20).
- Us: deliver a 2-page unit economics proposal and a sensitivity table showing $/1M at quantization/throughput ranges by Fri (4/22).
- Schedule: propose a technical deep-dive (30 min) with Marcus (product) and Monica (CS) to review sample payloads and latency/cost tradeoffs. I listed two slots in the calendar invite.

If that plan looks good I’ll finalize the workbook and draft an initial pricing appendix for procurement.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0128

Attachment: unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightpathhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers: 

1) Token split — ballpark is close to what you guessed: Search ~7.5M/mo, Summarization ~8.5M/mo, Recommendations ~4M/mo (total ~20M). These are production-first estimates; we expect Search tokens to grow faster.
2) Use contribution per converted user (we track downstream revenue per converted MAU after activation). Procurement wants to see CAC payback on that metric.
3) Procurement target: their preferred benchmark is $10/1M tokens or lower, but leadership has said they can consider up to $13 if the feature economics hold and there is strong SLAs.
4) Hosting: US-only for now; we will require SOC2 evidence and customer-managed audit logs during contract.

I’ll fill the top sheet in the workbook and return by EOD Tue. Can you provide a very quick sensitivity table that shows net margin at $8, $10, $12, and $15 per 1M tokens? That will be helpful for our finance presentation.

—Elena
Elena Kuznetsov
Head of Product Ops | BrightPath Health
elena.k@brightpathhealth.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the target guidance. I attached a proposal workbook (BP-unit-econ-proposal.xlsx) with the sensitivity table you asked for. Short explanation of the assumptions so finance has context: 

Key cost assumptions (baseline)
- Redwood inference cost to serve (baseline model + standard batching): $4.20 per 1M tokens
- Additional Ops/KMS/audit amortized: $0.60 per 1M tokens
- Expected delivery overhead (feature-specific preprocess + postprocess compute): varies by feature; we modeled Search at +$1.10, Summarization +$0.90, Recs +$0.50 per 1M tokens

Net unit cost (examples)
- Search: $6.90 / 1M tokens
- Summarization: $5.70 / 1M tokens
- Recommendations: $5.30 / 1M tokens

Suggested commercial framing
- List price bands by token tier with a target margin: we recommend a target gross margin of 55–65% for feature pricing to maintain room for discounts and committed capacity. That implies list $/1M tokens in the $12–$15 range for Search (higher consumption) and $10–$13 for Summarization/Recs.

CAC payback example (simple)
- If contribution per converted user = $120/year and feature drives 0.8 conversions per 1k MAU, then annual contribution per 1k MAU ≈ $96. At $12/1M tokens and 20M tokens/mo across the product, you can model payback windows. I included a tab that lets you plug your exact contribution and conversion numbers.

Attachments: BP-unit-econ-proposal.xlsx (contains the sensitivity table), mutual_action_plan.pdf (draft MAM with milestones, including SOC2 evidence delivery).

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive (30 min): Wed 4/21 9:00–9:30am PT or Thu 4/22 10:00–10:30am PT. Marcus — can you confirm availability? Monica will cover onboarding and support ramp.

Will prepare a one-page slide (pricing appendix) for procurement after the call so you have a clean ask number.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: BP-unit-econ-proposal.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps

Thanks — I’m available for the Thu 4/22 10:00–10:30am PT slot. A couple of engineering notes we should call out in the deep-dive so BrightPath understands sensitivity: 
- Model variant: switching from baseline to a quantized Llama variant can reduce inference compute by ~30–40%, lowering the $/1M token line by ~1.4–1.8 in our baseline assumptions.
- Batching improvements: if BrightPath accepts a slightly higher latency for batchable calls (e.g., background summary jobs), we can push cost down further.
- Caching: prefix and KV caching for user session contexts can dramatically reduce tokens per logical query for Summarization — I added a short note in the proposal workbook.

I’ll join Thu and prepare a concise slide that maps the tech levers to delta $/1M tokens.

—Marcus
Director, Product | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@brightpathhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Feature-level unit economics follow-up and next steps

Camila / Marcus — thanks, the Thu slot works. For the finance briefing I need a single recommended list price to present with the sensitivity table. Based on your workbook, can you confirm a recommended list $/1M tokens (single number) that you think is defensible for BrightPath given our volume and US-only SOC2 requirement? Procurement prefers a whole-dollar number.

If you can provide that by EOD Thu (4/22) that’d be ideal — we’ll use it in our internal deck.

Thanks,
Elena
